reforms.description: The 2010 federal budget announced a comprehensive review of all federal support for research and development to improve its contribution to innovation.
reforms.component_name: Comprehensive review of federal R&D support
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: A comprehensive review of federal R&D support aimed at improving innovation contribution is expected to enhance research productivity and allocative efficiency in the public research system.
reforms.importance_rationale: A comprehensive review of all federal R&D support is significant and system-wide in scope, but the announcement of a review is less concrete than implementation of specific reforms.
reforms.source_quote: The 2010 federal budget announced a comprehensive review of all federal support for research and development to improve its contribution to innovation.
reforms.cross_verification_note: The comprehensive review of federal support for research and development aims to improve its contribution to innovation, indicating a focus on R&D funding.

reforms.description: Two tax treaty and tax code reforms removed barriers to venture capital flows: the 2008 Fifth Protocol to the Canada-US Tax Treaty introduced rules ensuring hybrid entity income is treated as earned by a resident of the residence country for treaty purposes; and Budget 2010 narrowed the definition of taxable Canadian property under the Income Tax Act to eliminate tax reporting requirements for non-residents on many equity investments.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Removing tax barriers to venture capital flows reduces friction in the startup financing ecosystem, lowering the cost of capital for innovative firms and supporting the commercialisation and scaling of new ventures.
reforms.status_evidence: Both reforms are described as implemented: the Fifth Protocol was ratified in 2008, and Budget 2010 announced the narrowing of taxable Canadian property definition with status 'implemented'.
reforms.importance_rationale: These are targeted but meaningful reforms addressing specific tax barriers to venture capital. They are narrower than system-wide R&D reforms but significant for the startup ecosystem.
reforms.source_quote: The Fifth Protocol to the Canada-US Tax Treaty, ratified in 2008, introduced rules designed to ensure that income that the residents of one country earn through a hybrid entity (such as a limited liability corporation) will, in certain cases, be treated by the other country as having been earned by a resident of the residence country for purposes of the treaty.
reforms.cross_verification_note: The tax treaty and tax code reforms aim to facilitate venture capital flows, which can support innovation instruments for R&D-intensive firms.

all_reforms_including_excluded.description: The federal government has invested over CAD10 billion since 2006 to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and promote sustainable environmental practices through investments in green infrastructure, energy efficiency, and clean-energy technologies.
all_reforms_including_excluded.growth_orientation_rationale: Investments in green technologies are expected to foster innovation in sustainable practices and contribute to economic growth.
all_reforms_including_excluded.status_evidence: The investment has been ongoing since 2006.
all_reforms_including_excluded.importance_rationale: This reform represents a significant investment in R&D for environmental sustainability, marking a major policy shift.
all_reforms_including_excluded.source_quote: Since 2006, the Government of Canada has invested more than CAD10 billion to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and build a more sustainable environment through investments in green infrastructure, energy efficiency and clean-energy technologies.
all_reforms_including_excluded.cross_verification_note: The description focuses on investments in green infrastructure and clean-energy technologies, which do not qualify as R&D funding or knowledge transfer.

all_reforms_including_excluded.description: Ontario proposed to complete the phase-out of its tax credit for Labour-Sponsored Investment Funds by 2012.
all_reforms_including_excluded.growth_orientation_rationale: The phase-out of this tax credit may reduce incentives for investment in certain funds, potentially hindering innovation.
all_reforms_including_excluded.status_evidence: The proposal has been made but not yet implemented.
all_reforms_including_excluded.importance_rationale: This reform is a minor adjustment to existing tax policy rather than a major overhaul.
all_reforms_including_excluded.source_quote: Ontario proposed to complete the phase-out of its tax credit for Labour-Sponsored Investment Funds by 2012.
all_reforms_including_excluded.cross_verification_note: The reform discusses the phase-out of a tax credit, but does not indicate a new innovation instrument or R&D funding mechanism.

all_reforms_including_excluded.description: Canada is promoting the application of information and communication technologies (ICT) in health care to improve quality and cost-efficiency, including the use of electronic health records (EHR). Additionally, the establishment of an independent, pan-Canadian agency to monitor health-care quality and provide advice on best practices is proposed to enhance accountability and improve health outcomes. A comprehensive review of all federal support for research and development is also announced to improve its contribution to innovation.
all_reforms_including_excluded.growth_orientation_rationale: The integration of ICT in health care is expected to enhance efficiency and quality, leading to better health outcomes and potentially reducing costs.
all_reforms_including_excluded.status_evidence: The reforms are proposed and have not yet been implemented.
all_reforms_including_excluded.importance_rationale: The reforms involve significant changes in health care delivery and monitoring, but do not constitute a major overhaul of the system.
all_reforms_including_excluded.source_quote: Creating an independent, pan-Canadian agency to explicitly monitor health-care quality and provide advice on clinical and institutional best practice could importantly support this work.
all_reforms_including_excluded.cross_verification_note: While it mentions a review of federal support for R&D, the primary focus is on ICT in health care, which does not clearly indicate a direct R&D funding mechanism.

all_reforms_including_excluded.description: The 2010 federal budget announced the removal of existing restrictions on foreign ownership of Canadian communications satellites, consistent with recommendations to lift restrictions on foreign direct investment.
all_reforms_including_excluded.component_name: Foreign ownership restrictions on communications satellites
all_reforms_including_excluded.growth_orientation_rationale: Removal of foreign ownership restrictions on communications satellites may support growth through increased investment and competition, but the primary mechanism is regulatory liberalisation rather than innovation policy. The innovation relevance is indirect and uncertain.
all_reforms_including_excluded.importance_rationale: This is a regulatory change affecting foreign investment in a specific sector (communications satellites), not a core innovation policy reform. It is narrowly scoped and incremental.
all_reforms_including_excluded.source_quote: Consistent with the recommendations of the Competition Policy Review Panel, the 2010 federal budget announced the removal of existing restrictions on foreign ownership of Canadian communications satellites.
all_reforms_including_excluded.cross_verification_note: The reform concerns the removal of restrictions on foreign ownership, which is unrelated to R&D funding or knowledge transfer.
